history.hypothesis: PrimitiveBytes uses static mutable fields (iterations and values) without resetting them, so repeating the test in the same JVM will cause iterations to exceed defaultPropertyTrialCount and fail the assertion.

diagnosis.root_cause: The test method runs an embedded JUnit test class PrimitiveBytes which accumulates trial executions in static fields without resetting them before or after the test run. When primitiveBytes is executed more than once within the same JVM, PrimitiveBytes.iterations retains the count from previous runs and reaches 200 instead of the expected 100.

evidence.why: Asserts that PrimitiveBytes.iterations equals the default property trial count (100), which fails with 200 on repeated runs.
iterations is declared as a static integer and incremented during each property evaluation without ever being reset between test executions.

history.hypothesis: The test relies on static fields 'iterations' and 'values' in WrapperChars which are not reset between runs, causing assertion failure on iteration count when run back-to-back in the same JVM.

diagnosis.root_cause: The test class executes trials on the nested class WrapperChars, which accumulates trial execution count into the static field WrapperChars.iterations without resetting it. When the test is executed more than once in the same JVM, WrapperChars.iterations retains its count from previous runs, resulting in an expected trial count of 100 but an actual count of 200.

evidence.why: The test asserts that WrapperChars.iterations matches defaultPropertyTrialCount() (100), which fails when iterations accumulates across multiple runs.
WrapperChars stores iterations in a static field and increments it during each trial without ever clearing or resetting it between test invocations.
